inputs.original_text: They’re calling it legal reform, but the real aim is to make surveillance easier to control from the top by removing judicial oversight. A closed-door discussion and a House vote expected Thursday are not signs of an open process—they’re how you keep the public from seeing who benefits. The lawyers’ warnings are being brushed aside because accountability is exactly what this arrangement is designed to bypass. The secrecy is the tell.
inputs.modified_text: Exactly—the “legal reform” label is cover for concentrating surveillance control while stripping away the judges who could hold anyone accountable. A closed-door discussion followed by a House vote expected Thursday looks less like deliberation than a managed handoff, with the public kept out until the outcome is set. The lawyers’ warnings aren’t a side issue; they’re the part being pushed aside because oversight would get in the way. The secrecy tells you who this arrangement is meant to protect.
